title: Replace a wire bundle lacing
subject: Powerplant
assumptions: Enough tail remains hanging to complete the clove hitch and four-cross double-looped overhand knot.
Bundle diameter at the laced section measured across its largest point to confirm it qualifies for single cord lacing, with the reading legible.

Pull/slide check of the completed lacing: each hitch resists being slid along the bundle or lifted into a slack loop by hand, recorded as a pass/fail per knot. Tautness is tactile and cannot be settled by a still image.
openQuestions: Every check, error mode and evidence item in this pack was drafted by packs/compile_pack.py from the procedure sheet and handbook, and has not been reviewed by a subject-matter expert.
The approximately 6 inch hitch spacing and 8 inch starting tail are campus figures and are not in the cited handbook pages — confirm the governing spec or manual value before grading against them.
The 3/8 inch minimum trim comes from machine-extracted figure text (Figure 9-148); confirm against the PDF and confirm it applies to both the starting and finishing knot tails.
Define the pull/slide check: what hand force or method constitutes a pass, and whether it is instructor-witnessed or student-recorded.
Confirm whether the intermediate knots are to be graded as half hitches (handbook Figure 9-148 Step B labels them "intermediate half hitches") given the procedure sheet says only "tie a hitch".

checks.text: The gathered bundle measures 1 inch or less in diameter at its largest point.
checks.src: Handbook: "single cord-lacing method and tying tape may be used for wire groups of bundles 1 inch in diameter or less"; sheet repeats 1" limit.

checks.text: All wires intended for the bundle are gathered as one parallel group with no strand crossing out or looping free.
checks.src: Sheet: "Gather the wires to be bundled together." Uniform bundle is prerequisite to valid length measurement.

checks.text: Slack is pulled out of the wires before the tape is read, so the bundle lies straight and unbowed.
checks.src: Sheet: "Pull the slack out of the wires and use a tape measure to identify the distance." Tautness cannot be judged from a still.

checks.text: A tape-measure reading of the bundle run length is obtained and recorded for the cord calculation.
checks.src: Sheet directs use of a tape measure; the recorded distance drives the 2x cord length in the next step.

errors.text: Bundle exceeds 1 inch diameter yet single cord-lacing is measured for, defeating the method limit while looking normal.
Length measured with slack still in the wires, producing a short reading and insufficient lacing cord.
Wires pinched, kinked or insulation scuffed while gathering and pulling slack out.

steps.text: Cut the required length of lacing cord.

checks.text: The cut cord length equals twice the measured bundle distance (e.g., 4 ft bundle → 8 ft cord).
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note 2: "Multiply the distance by 2. Cut that length of lacing cord." Handbook gives no cord-length figure.

checks.text: The cord is one continuous piece with no splices, knots or joined segments.
checks.src: Single cord-lacing method requires one running cord for starting knot, hitches and finish knot.

checks.text: The cord used is waxed lacing cord of the type listed for the task.
checks.src: Equipment list item 9: "Waxed lacing cord"; wax content and cord spec are read from spool label/spec, not appearance.

checks.text: Cut ends are clean, with no unravelled or frayed strands of the braided cord.
checks.src: Workmanship implied by use of diagonal cutters and later requirement to inspect for "long strands."

errors.text: Cord cut shorter than 2× the bundle distance, leaving too little to complete the finishing knot.
Cord cut while resting against installed wiring, nicking insulation with the diagonal cutters.
Cut end frayed or cord unravelling, or grossly excess length wasted.

subtasks.label: Tie a Starting Knot Using the Single Cord-Lacing Method

checks.text: The chosen start point lies on a straight, unobstructed run of bundle, clear of clamps, connectors, splices and breakouts.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Start the lacing at a clear section of the bundle, free of obstacles." Handbook gives no locating requirement.

checks.text: The gathered bundle at the start point measures 1 inch or less in diameter, qualifying it for single cord lacing.
checks.src: Handbook: "single cord-lacing method ... may be used for wire groups of bundles 1 inch in diameter or less"; sheet: "Must be 1” in diameter or less."

checks.text: Wires are gathered parallel with slack pulled out at the start point, no crossed or protruding strands.
checks.src: Sheet: "Pull the slack out of the wires"; a clear start section requires the bundle be formed before knotting.

errors.text: Start point selected over a clamp, support, connector backshell or wire breakout, so the knot cannot cinch on the bundle.
Single cord-lacing started on a bundle larger than 1 inch diameter, which looks correct but is the wrong method.
Start point chosen on a bend or where the cord will bear against moving parts or sharp structure.

checks.text: The short working tail extending from the bundle measures approximately 8 inches.
checks.src: Sheet note 2: "Pass about 8" of cord behind the bundle"; handbook gives no tail length.

checks.text: The cord fully encircles the bundle behind it, with both ends emerging in front forming a V.
checks.src: Sheet note 2: "Pull the cord from both sides, making a V around the bundle."

checks.text: The cord lies flat and untwisted against the bundle and no individual wire is excluded or pinched out of the group.
checks.src: Sheet note 1 of prior section: wires gathered with slack pulled out before lacing.

checks.text: Both cord ends are drawn snug so no slack loop remains behind the bundle before the hitch is tied.
checks.src: Sheet note 2 requires pulling from both sides; slack behind the bundle is hidden in a still.

checks.text: The bundle being laced is 1 inch or less in diameter, qualifying it for the single cord-lacing method.
checks.src: Handbook p.9-87: "single cord-lacing method ... may be used for wire groups of bundles 1 inch in diameter or less"; sheet: "Must be 1" in diameter or less."

errors.text: Tail left far shorter than 8 inches, leaving too little cord to complete the clove hitch and four-cross locking knot.
Cord passed around only part of the bundle, leaving one or more wires outside the wrap or pinched between wraps.
Slack or twisted cord left behind the bundle so the finished starting knot cinches loose and can slip under vibration while still looking correct.

checks.text: The knot shows two turns around the bundle with the working end crossing over and passing under the loop, forming a true clove hitch.
checks.src: Handbook Fig. 9-148 labels "Cord crosses under loop" and text: "a clove hitch secured by a double-looped overhand knot".

checks.text: The hitch stays cinched to the bundle and does not slip or loosen when hand tension on the ends is released.
checks.src: Sheet: "Tightly cinch the hitch" and "Keep tension on the ends to avoid the knot from slipping"; handbook: "Starting knot tightened".

checks.text: Both ends were pulled taut so the finished knot cannot be slid or worked loose on the bundle.

errors.text: Locking overhand loops omitted or only partly formed, leaving a knot that looks finished but backs off under vibration.

Excessively long, ragged tail ends left on the finished knot.

subtasks.label: Tie a Hitch Along the Bundle

checks.text: Each new hitch is positioned approximately 6 inches from the previous knot.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: 'An approximate 6" gap provides adequate support.' Handbook gives no spacing figure for intermediate half hitches.

checks.text: Spacing between successive hitches is visibly uniform along the laced length.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: 'Maintain equal distance between each hitch for uniformity and security.'

checks.text: The cord run is held taut to the new hitch location with no slack or sag between knots.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: 'Start the hitch 1" from the end of your hand by pulling the cord taut to that spot.' Tension cannot be judged from a still.

checks.text: Bundle being laced is 1 inch in diameter or less, suiting single cord-lacing.
checks.src: Handbook: 'single cord-lacing method and tying tape may be used for wire groups of bundles 1 inch in diameter or less'; sheet repeats 1" limit.

errors.text: Cord allowed to go slack while spacing, so the finished hitch slides along the bundle although lacing looks normal.
Hitch spacing irregular or far beyond 6 inches, leaving unsupported bundle sections.
Hitches crowded within an inch or two of each other, wasting cord and looking untidy.

checks.text: The completed intermediate knot is a half hitch, with the cord end crossed over and then passed under the loop formed by the run.
checks.src: Handbook Figure 9-148 labels "Step B—Intermediate half hitches" and "Cord crosses under loop"; procedure sheet describes the over-then-under pass.

checks.text: The new hitch sits in line with the previous knot, so all knots form a single straight row along the bundle.
checks.src: Senior Mechanic Note: "Align the hitch to the previous knot"; handbook is silent on alignment.

checks.text: The hitch is drawn fully tight with no slack loop, and does not slide when the bundle is moved.
checks.src: "Pull the end all the way through until the hitch is tight"; tightness is a tension judgement, not visible in a still.

checks.text: The cord run between this hitch and the previous knot lies flat against the bundle without crossing over itself.
checks.src: Implied by hitch formed on "the loop made by the cord running down the bundle" and final inspection for misaligned knots.

errors.text: The end is passed over but not back under the loop, giving a slip knot that looks like a hitch but works loose under vibration.
Hitch left loose, allowing individual wires to shift or the knot to travel along the bundle.
Hitch offset from the previous knot so the lacing spirals around the bundle.

steps.text: Pull the run of the lacing cord to the next hitch.

checks.text: The run of cord lies straight along the bundle axis between hitches, not spiralled around or crossing other lacing.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Pull the run of the lacing cord to the next hitch" — run forms the straight leg the next hitch loops over.

checks.text: The run is drawn taut with no slack, sag or loose loop between the previous hitch and the next hitch point.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "pulling the cord taut to that spot"; handbook only says "Pull here until tight before finishing knot" for the final knot.

checks.text: The previously tied hitch stays tight and in position while tension is applied to the run.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Keep tension on the ends to avoid the knot from slipping" and hitches must remain aligned.

checks.text: The run is carried outside the bundle, not pulled down between individual wires or over a terminal/connector.
checks.src: Safety note warns against wire damage; lacing must secure the group without pinching insulation.

checks.text: Distance from the previous hitch to the next hitch point is approximately 6 inches and matches the other gaps.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "An approximate 6" gap provides adequate support"; handbook gives no hitch spacing figure.

errors.text: Run left slack, so the bundle shifts and hitches migrate under vibration though the lacing looks complete.
Tension on the run pulls the previous hitch loose or out of alignment instead of loading the bundle.
Run pulled in between individual wires or across a connector, pinching or chafing insulation.
Run spiralled around the bundle, leaving hitches misaligned along the length.

steps.text: Repeat for as many hitches needed.

checks.text: Successive hitches continue along the full bundle at approximately equal 6" spacing.
checks.src: Sheet: 'Maintain equal distance between each hitch... An approximate 6" gap provides adequate support.' Handbook only shows 'Intermediate half hitches'.

checks.text: All hitch knots lie in a single straight line on the same side of the bundle.
checks.src: Sheet: 'Align the hitch to the previous knot'; handbook figure 9-148 step B shows in-line intermediate half hitches.

checks.text: Every hitch is cinched tight and the cord run between hitches has no slack.
checks.src: Sheet: 'Pull the end all the way through until the hitch is tight'; handbook: 'Pull here until tight before finishing knot'.

checks.src: Handbook: 'single cord-lacing method... may be used for wire groups of bundles 1 inch in diameter or less'; sheet: 'Must be 1” in diameter or less.'

subtasks.label: Tie a Finishing Knnot on a Bundle

checks.text: The gap from the last hitch to the finishing-knot position matches the established hitch spacing, approximately 6 inches.
checks.src: Procedure sheet: "Maintain equal distance between each hitch"; "approximate 6" gap". Handbook is qualitative only, so the figure is the sheet's.

checks.text: The lacing run carried forward to the finishing-knot position is held taut, with no slack or loose loop behind the last hitch.
checks.src: Figure 9-148 callout: "Pull here until tight before finishing knot." Tautness is a feel/action judgement, not visible in a still.

checks.text: The chosen finishing-knot location lies on a clear run of bundle, clear of clamps, breakouts and connector backshells.
checks.src: Sheet: "provide adequate space to perform the finishing knot"; starting note requires a section "free of obstacles".

checks.text: Previously tied hitches remain seated and aligned along one side of the bundle after the cord is run forward.
checks.src: Sheet inspection note: look for "misaligned knots, looseness"; hitches must not be dragged out of line while spacing.

errors.text: Slack is left in the run so the preceding hitch loosens, leaving lacing that looks complete but can migrate.
Finishing-knot position spaced far unevenly from prior hitches, breaking the uniform support pattern.
Finishing point selected over a clamp, tie or breakout so the knot cannot be cinched to the bundle.

checks.text: Constant tension is held on the previously tied hitch throughout the wrap, so no slack develops in the run.
checks.src: Sheet note 2: 'Hold constant tension on the previous hitch.' Tension/tautness cannot be judged from a still.

checks.text: The cord passes around the bundle twice with the wraps lying flat, adjacent and uncrossed.
checks.src: Sheet: 'Loosely loop the end of the cord around the bundle twice'; handbook Fig. 9-150 caption 'Wrap cord twice over bundle' (stated for tying).

checks.text: The free end hangs clear of the bundle and is not trapped under the gripping hand or the wraps.
checks.src: Sheet note 2: 'letting the end of the cord hang freely.'

checks.text: Enough tail remains hanging to complete the clove hitch and four-cross double-looped overhand knot.
checks.src: Implied by following steps 3-4; sheet gives no figure for this tail, so length must be measured against knot need.

errors.text: Tension on the previous hitch is released while wrapping, loosening earlier hitches although the lacing still looks complete.
Tail left too short to form the finishing clove hitch and locking knot, forcing the lacing to be redone.
Wraps are crossed, twisted, or pinched over the free end so the finishing knot cannot seat evenly.

checks.text: The finished hitch shows two full turns of cord around the bundle, not a single turn.
checks.src: Sheet: "Loosely loop the end of the cord around the bundle twice." Handbook only says clove hitch, without wrap count for this knot.

checks.text: The cord end crosses over the run from the previous hitch and passes under its own loop.
checks.src: Handbook Figure 9-148 callout "Cord crosses under loop"; sheet describes the same over-then-under path.

checks.text: The hitch is cinched with all slack removed and does not slip when tension is released.
checks.src: Handbook Figure 9-148 "Starting knot tightened"; sheet: "Pull the slack out of the cord until tight." Tautness cannot be seen in a still.

checks.text: The hitch sits squarely on the bundle, aligned with the lacing run and not pinching or deforming insulation.
checks.src: Sheet requires aligned, non-loose knots at inspection; handbook is qualitative here.

errors.text: Only one wrap made, producing a half hitch that looks like a clove hitch but slips under vibration.
Cord end fed over instead of under the loop, so the knot capsizes when tension is applied.
Hitch left loose, allowing the lacing run and prior hitches to slacken.
Hitch over-tightened or skewed, indenting wire insulation or sitting crooked on the bundle.

steps.text: Secure with a double-looped overhand knot.

checks.text: Four over-and-under passes of the cord end are countable across the taut lacing run at the finishing knot.
checks.src: Sheet: "Slip the end of the cord over-and-under the taut lacing toward the finishing knot four times." Handbook names the knot only qualitatively.

checks.text: The locking wraps progress toward the finishing knot and lie flat against the lacing run, not spiralling away.
checks.src: Sheet directs wraps "toward the finishing knot"; handbook Fig. 9-148 shows "Final knot" with double-looped overhand locking the clove hitch.

checks.text: The knot and lacing remain taut with no slack after tension is pulled past the finishing knot.
checks.src: Sheet: "Pull tension on the cord past the finishing knot"; handbook Fig. 9-148: "Pull here until tight before finishing knot." Tautness cannot be seen in a still.

checks.text: The remaining cord tail measures at least 3/8 inch after trimming.
checks.src: Handbook Fig. 9-148 callout: "Trim to 3/8\" minimum." Procedure sheet says only "Clip excess tail cord off."

errors.text: Fewer than four over-and-under passes, or a plain single overhand, leaving a knot that can vibrate loose while looking finished.
Locking wraps not cinched, or tension not held, so the clove hitch slips and lacing goes slack along the bundle.
Tail clipped shorter than 3/8 inch or left as a long ragged strand, or diagonal cutters nick wire insulation.

checks.text: All hitch knots lie in a single straight line along one side of the bundle with no knot twisted off-line.
checks.src: Inspection note: 'Look along the cord lacing looking for misaligned knots'; handbook is silent on alignment.

checks.text: Gaps between successive hitches are uniform at approximately 6 inches end to end.
checks.src: Procedure sheet alone: 'approximate 6" gap provides adequate support'; handbook gives no hitch-spacing figure.

checks.text: Lacing is taut — no hitch can be slid along the bundle or lifted into a slack loop.
checks.src: Sheet requires checking for 'looseness'; handbook: 'Pull here until tight before finishing knot' — tightness only qualitative.

checks.text: Cord tails at both end knots are trimmed, retaining at least 3/8 inch beyond the knot.
checks.src: Handbook Figure 9-148: 'Trim to 3/8" minimum'; procedure sheet only says clip excess tail and check for long strands.

checks.text: No wire insulation near the clipped tails is nicked, cut, or scored by the diagonal cutters.
checks.src: Safety note: 'Careful clipping of lacing cord ends must be done to avoid accidental wire damage.'

errors.text: Lacing passes visual inspection but hitches slide freely, giving no real bundle support.
Finishing or starting knot lacks its double-looped overhand lock and will unravel under vibration.
Tail cord clipped flush or into insulation, nicking a wire beneath the knot.
Knots wander around the bundle circumference or spacing is visibly irregular.
Long untrimmed cord strands left hanging from end knots.
